label: accepted

evidence.V1: Stone wall with a framed cross-mullion window reads at all angles; slab silhouette is appropriate for a modular wall piece.
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: cap course and dark plinth course, stone blocks, window frame, mullion cross and gold keystone.
evidence.V3: Competent but stiff: window is small and squat for an 8x12 wall, block pattern is regular with little stylised variation.
evidence.V4: Consistent ~0.06-stud chamfers on blocks, sill, frame and cap catch the light (sill and end_section close-ups).
evidence.V5: Frame jambs stop short of the sill leaving visible gaps, and the keystone notches into the lintel/glass (window flat close-up).
evidence.V6: Stone grey in about three values with timber mullion and one gold accent; brick/sandstone colourways stay disciplined.
evidence.V8: Matches the modular brief: stone hue, timber secondary, gold keystone, one white vertex-colour material, chamfered edges, T1 tiling pass on the 2-stud grid.
evidence.V9: Modular piece: Anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner origin.

artifacts: Gaps between window jambs and sill (window flat close-up)
Keystone intersects lintel and glass with a visible notch
top_fixes: Close the jambs down onto the sill and seat the keystone cleanly on the lintel
Enlarge the window (taller opening) so it carries the 8x12 wall face
Add a little irregularity to the block sizes/offsets for a more stylised read
